1.summary: AI is any system that performs tasks that normally need human cognition, and ML is the part of AI that learns patterns from data. This lesson separates ML from business intelligence and shows which business problems ML suits, especially those involving unstructured data.
objectives: Define AI and machine learning in business terms
Distinguish ML (learn and predict) from BI (report on the past)
Recognize good ML use cases such as recommendations, churn and sentiment from audio
Spot tasks ML is a poor fit for
Tell descriptive analytics, predictive analytics, supervised and unsupervised learning apart
takeaways: AI = tasks that need human cognition. ML = learns from data to make predictions or decisions.
BI uses dashboards and reports on historical data. ML predicts and automates.
Descriptive analytics reports what happened. Predictive analytics forecasts. AI is the broad field, with ML, deep learning and gen AI inside it.
Unstructured data such as audio, images and free text is where ML adds unique value.
Predict churn by training a model on customers who already left.
Supervised learning uses labeled examples. Unsupervised learning finds groupings in unlabeled data.
ML needs past examples to learn from and should not make final ethical decisions.
Google Cloud offers AI tools for every skill level, from APIs to custom training.

2.summary: Model quality depends on data quality and quantity. This lesson covers why more training data improves accuracy, why inconsistent sources must be transformed first, and why combined, representative data beats narrow slices.
objectives: Explain why more and better training data improves prediction accuracy
Prepare inconsistent data by transforming it into a consistent format
Describe why training data should be combined and representative
List the common data preparation steps and why full history matters
takeaways: To improve accuracy, add more relevant, good-quality training data. Storage, bandwidth and CPU speed don't help.
Different column names and date formats? Transform to one consistent format before training.
Preparation means standardizing dates, field names, types and categories, handling missing values and removing duplicates. Keep the full history for seasonality.
Combine related datasets before predicting.
Training data should cover all conditions the model will see, not only extreme cases.

3.summary: Google Cloud offers a spectrum from pre-trained APIs and pre-built agents to BigQuery ML, AutoML and fully custom training. This lesson teaches how to pick a point on that spectrum and the speed-versus-differentiation tradeoff behind it.
objectives: Order the AI options from least to most effort
Match team skills and data to the right approach
Explain the tradeoff between pre-built and custom solutions
takeaways: Pre-built APIs and agents are fastest but give less business differentiation.
Custom models need more effort and expertise but give the most differentiation.
Pre-trained APIs cover common tasks. Predicting from your own business data needs a model trained on it.
SQL plus BigQuery means BigQuery ML. Labeled data with no ML coders means AutoML.
Neither approach shifts spending to CapEx or guarantees 100% accuracy.

4.summary: Pre-trained APIs give ready-made ML through a simple API call with no training. This lesson maps common inputs (photos, audio, text, video, scanned forms) to the Vision, Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Translation, Natural Language, Video Intelligence and Document AI services, plus Sensitive Data Protection for card numbers and personal data.
objectives: Choose the correct pre-trained API for images, audio, translation and text analysis
Explain why pre-trained APIs speed up AI adoption
Tell generic pre-trained labeling apart from custom AutoML categories
takeaways: Generic labels, objects, landmarks and text in photos mean Vision API.
Card numbers or ID data in photos: Vision OCR plus Sensitive Data Protection, no training needed.
Audio to text means Speech-to-Text. Text into other languages means Translation API.
Topics and sentiment in written text mean Natural Language API.
Document AI extracts key-value pairs, entities and tables from forms, invoices and receipts. Video Intelligence handles video, not photos.
Scanned forms become searchable text with extracted fields through APIs such as Document AI.
Pre-trained APIs remove the need for ML specialists, not for input data or permissions.

5.summary: When pre-trained APIs are not enough, Google Cloud offers three ways to build your own model. BigQuery ML uses SQL, AutoML trains on labeled data without code, and custom training runs data scientists' own code, often with TensorFlow.
objectives: Identify when BigQuery ML is the right choice
Identify when AutoML is the right choice for custom image or text categories
Recognize custom training and TensorFlow scenarios
Reject data-processing tools offered as ML answers
takeaways: Data in BigQuery plus SQL skills means BigQuery ML (CREATE MODEL), with no data export, even when AutoML is also offered.
Labeled examples in your own categories plus no ML coding skills means AutoML.
Data scientists writing training code means custom training: managed jobs with their own framework, containers and accelerators.
TensorFlow is Google's open-source, end-to-end ML platform. Apache Beam is a pipeline model and Dataflow runs it.
Predictive maintenance in BigQuery ML is a typical business-value example.

6.summary: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) is Google Cloud's unified, managed AI platform for the full ML lifecycle and for generative AI and agents. This lesson covers its scope, model choice through Model Garden, Agent Studio, the Agent Platform API and AI Hub.
objectives: Describe the ML lifecycle stages the platform manages
Explain the platform's model choice across Google, open and partner models
Match Agent Studio and the Agent Platform API to their use cases
Explain what AI Hub provides
takeaways: Prepare, train, deploy and monitor in one managed service means Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
It offers Google, open and third-party partner models through Model Garden.
Agent Studio is the no-code or low-code agent builder.
Call a finished agent from mobile or web apps through the Agent Platform API.
IAM controls who can call an agent, but the Agent Platform API is the interface.
GKE and Compute Engine can run ML but are not managed ML platforms.

7.summary: Generative AI creates new content from prompts, and foundation models are the large pre-trained models that make it possible. This lesson covers Gemini as Google's multimodal model and the real advantages and limits of foundation models.
objectives: Define generative AI and tell it apart from predictive analytics
Explain the strategic value of foundation models
Identify Gemini as Google's multimodal foundation model
Name the ways to adapt a foundation model and the risk of hallucinations
takeaways: Generative AI is a specific field of AI that creates content such as text, images, audio and code.
Foundation models give a pre-trained starting point that you can fine-tune, which cuts development time.
Adapt foundation models by prompting, grounding (RAG) or fine-tuning. Ungrounded output can hallucinate.
Gemini understands text, code, audio, images and video together.
Foundation models don't remove governance, don't make compute free and don't guarantee facts.

8.summary: Agentic AI goes beyond generating content. It plans, decides, calls tools and completes multi-step workflows. This lesson also covers Contact Center AI, Google's purpose-built solution for customer support, the Gemini Enterprise app, and the packaged AI solutions that appear as distractors.
objectives: Define agentic AI and distinguish it from generative AI and BI
Identify Google Cloud tools for building and calling agents
Choose Contact Center AI for customer-support scenarios
Recognize Document AI, Recommendations AI, Discovery AI for Retail and Cloud Talent Solution
takeaways: Agentic AI understands goals, plans, calls tools and completes workflows with little human input.
Generative AI creates content, and agentic AI takes actions.
Agent Studio, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and the Agent Platform API build and expose agents.
High-volume chat and phone support with routing, virtual agents, agent assist and personalization means Contact Center AI.
Talent Solution is for jobs, Discovery AI and Recommendations AI are for retail search and recommendations, Document AI is for documents.

9.summary: Training large models quickly needs specialized hardware. This lesson covers TPUs, GPUs, the AI Hypercomputer architecture and the world-leading AI differentiator.
objectives: Explain what TPUs are and when they are the answer
Describe AI Hypercomputer's components
Identify world-leading AI as a Google Cloud differentiator
takeaways: TPUs are Google's custom ASICs designed specifically for ML training, fast at tensor and matrix math.
For very large foundation models, use GPUs and TPUs.
AI Hypercomputer combines AI-optimized hardware, networking and storage, open software, ML frameworks and flexible consumption for training, tuning and serving.
Ready-to-use agents, Gemini models, the Gemini Enterprise app and a unified AI platform make up the world-leading AI differentiator.

10.summary: Responsible AI keeps AI systems fair, transparent, safe and private, and explainable AI shows why a model made a specific decision. Both are essential for trust and for regulated industries.
objectives: Define responsible AI and its core principles
Explain when explainable AI is required
Recognize where human oversight remains necessary
takeaways: Transparent, fair, safe, privacy-preserving and low-bias AI is responsible AI.
Explaining an individual decision to auditors calls for explainable AI, which also helps detect bias.
Bias often starts with unrepresentative training data.
Humans stay accountable for ethical decisions and for reviewing gen AI output.

glossary.definition: Programmatic interface to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for managing and calling deployed models and agents from code.
glossary.exam_context: Answer when a finished agent must be called from Android, iOS or web apps. IAM secures the call but isn't the interface. Billing and Storage APIs are distractors.

glossary.definition: No-code / low-code visual designer in the Google Cloud console for designing, configuring, testing and publishing AI agents.
glossary.exam_context: Answer when analysts without coding or ML skills must build agents. It doesn't train models on BigQuery tables.

glossary.definition: AI that understands a goal, plans, decides next steps, calls tools and completes multi-step workflows with minimal human involvement.
glossary.exam_context: Look for verbs like decide, trigger, update records, complete. Generative AI is the tempting wrong answer.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud repository of ready-to-use AI and ML resources such as models, notebooks and pipelines.
glossary.exam_context: It provides reusable resources. It doesn't serve predictions, write all your code or clean data. Dated product name.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud's integrated AI supercomputing architecture: performance-optimized hardware (TPUs, GPUs), networking and storage, open software, ML frameworks and flexible consumption models.
glossary.exam_context: Answer when a question lists hardware + open software + frameworks + flexible consumption for training, tuning and serving large models.

glossary.definition: Apache Beam is an open-source programming model for batch and streaming data pipelines. Dataflow is Google Cloud's managed service that runs Beam pipelines.
glossary.exam_context: Data processing, not an ML library. The open-source ML library answer is TensorFlow.

glossary.definition: Any system that can perform tasks that normally require human cognition.
glossary.exam_context: Not "any real-time system" or "any system that structures data".

glossary.definition: Trains a custom model on your labeled data without writing training code. Now AutoML on Agent Platform, formerly AutoML Vision and AutoML Natural Language.
glossary.exam_context: Labeled data + your own categories + no ML expertise. Generic labels go to the Vision API instead.

glossary.definition: Feature of BigQuery that creates and runs ML models with SQL where the data already lives.
glossary.exam_context: SQL-skilled analysts or DBAs, data in BigQuery, no data scientists, no export.

glossary.definition: Analysis of historical data through reports and dashboards.
glossary.exam_context: Describes the past. ML learns from data to predict and automate.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud AI service that improves job search and candidate matching for recruiting sites.
glossary.exam_context: Distractor in customer-support questions. It is about hiring, not support.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API that translates text between languages and can detect a text's language.
glossary.exam_context: Translate product pages into many languages. It doesn't transcribe audio or find topics.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud's purpose-built AI solution for customer service: virtual agents, intelligent routing, agent assist and conversation insights across chat and phone.
glossary.exam_context: High-volume chat/phone support that must stay personalized. Text-to-Speech or Recommendations AI alone don't fit.

glossary.definition: Training a model with your own code as managed jobs in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, with your choice of framework, containers and accelerators.
glossary.exam_context: Data scientists writing training code. Most effort, highest differentiation. Compute Engine would leave the infrastructure to you.

glossary.definition: Analysis that summarizes what already happened, through reports and dashboards.
glossary.exam_context: Doesn't predict or act. Distractor for agentic AI and ML questions.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud AI for retail product search, recommendations and personalization.
glossary.exam_context: Distractor for defect detection or custom image classification.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained service that uses OCR and extracts structured data (key-value pairs, entities, tables, fields) from documents such as forms, invoices, receipts and contracts.
glossary.exam_context: Scanned forms become searchable data. Not a general ML platform or a contact-center solution.

glossary.definition: Techniques that show why a model made a specific prediction.
glossary.exam_context: Regulated decisions (mortgages, credit) where auditors need the reason for each outcome.

glossary.definition: Further training a pre-trained foundation model on your own examples so it fits a specific task.
glossary.exam_context: One way to adapt a foundation model, alongside prompting and grounding.

glossary.definition: Large model pre-trained on broad data that can be prompted, grounded or fine-tuned for many tasks.
glossary.exam_context: Main advantage: a pre-trained starting point that cuts development time. It doesn't guarantee factual answers.

glossary.definition: Google's multimodal foundation model family that understands text, code, audio, images and video.
glossary.exam_context: Answer for "multimodal model" across many input types.

glossary.definition: Google's enterprise AI app (formerly Google Agentspace) where employees use Gemini models and ready-made or custom agents over company data.
glossary.exam_context: Part of the world-leading AI differentiator. Not the same as Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the developer platform.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud's unified, managed AI platform (formerly Vertex AI) for the full ML lifecycle, foundation models and agents.
glossary.exam_context: Prepare, train, deploy, monitor. Explore and adapt foundation models. Offers Google, open and partner models.

glossary.definition: Specific field of AI that creates new content such as text, images, audio, code and summaries from prompts.
glossary.exam_context: Creates content. Predictive analytics forecasts, and agentic AI acts.

glossary.definition: Graphics processing unit, a general-purpose accelerator widely used for ML training and inference.
glossary.exam_context: Paired with TPUs for training very large foundation models.

glossary.definition: Connecting a model's answers to trusted sources, such as search or your own documents. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fetches relevant content and adds it to the prompt.
glossary.exam_context: Reduces hallucinations and adapts foundation models to company data without retraining.

glossary.definition: Generative AI output that sounds confident but is false, incomplete or outdated.
glossary.exam_context: Why foundation models don't guarantee accuracy and still need grounding and human review.

glossary.definition: Subset of AI in which systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions, improving with more data. Deep learning and generative AI sit inside it.
glossary.exam_context: Recommendations, churn prediction, image classification. Not suited to tasks with no past patterns or ethical final decisions.

glossary.definition: Catalog in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for discovering and using Google, open and third-party partner models.
glossary.exam_context: Answer for model choice across providers. It has largely taken over AI Hub's role.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API for sentiment, entities, syntax and content classification in text.
glossary.exam_context: Find main topics in chat transcripts. Speech must be transcribed first.

glossary.definition: Ready-made Google ML models called through an API, with no training needed.
glossary.exam_context: Fastest option, no ML specialists needed, less differentiation.

glossary.definition: Using historical and current data to forecast likely outcomes, such as churn or demand.
glossary.exam_context: Forecasts, but doesn't create content. Distractor for generative AI questions.

glossary.definition: Packaged Google Cloud solution for personalized product and content recommendations.
glossary.exam_context: Not a contact center, not a general ML platform, not a text classifier.

glossary.definition: Practice of building AI that is transparent, fair, safe, privacy-preserving and accountable and that reduces harmful bias.
glossary.exam_context: Answer when a company defines principles to keep trust in its AI.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud service (formerly Cloud DLP) that discovers, classifies and redacts sensitive data such as payment card numbers and personal information.
glossary.exam_context: With Vision OCR, flags ID or payment cards in uploaded photos without training a model.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API that transcribes audio into text.
glossary.exam_context: Transcribe call recordings before sentiment analysis.

glossary.definition: Training a model on labeled examples so it learns to predict the label for new data.
glossary.exam_context: AutoML image classification on labeled photos is supervised learning.

glossary.definition: Google's open-source machine learning library with a large ecosystem of tools and community.
glossary.exam_context: Answer for "open-source ML library". Apache Beam and Dataflow are data processing.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API that turns text into natural-sounding spoken audio.
glossary.exam_context: The reverse of Speech-to-Text. One building block, not a full contact center.

glossary.definition: Google's custom ASIC designed specifically to accelerate machine learning workloads, especially tensor and matrix math.
glossary.exam_context: "Hardware designed for ML" or "domain-specific hardware" to cut training time.

glossary.definition: The examples a model learns from. Its quantity, quality and representativeness drive accuracy.
glossary.exam_context: More relevant, good-quality training data improves accuracy. Transform inconsistent sources first and keep the full history.

glossary.definition: Data that doesn't fit rows and columns, such as audio, images, video and free text.
glossary.exam_context: Sentiment from call audio is the classic ML-on-unstructured-data example.

glossary.definition: Finding structure, such as groupings, in data without labels.
glossary.exam_context: Still needs real patterns in the data. With no useful patterns, ML is a poor fit.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API that detects labels, objects, shots and explicit content in video.
glossary.exam_context: For video only. Still photos go to Vision API or AutoML.

glossary.definition: Pre-trained API that detects labels, objects, landmarks, logos, faces and text in images.
glossary.exam_context: Generic image tagging without training. Custom categories go to AutoML.

glossary.definition: Google Cloud differentiator covering ready-to-use agents, first-party models like Gemini and a unified AI platform.
glossary.exam_context: Not global network, open standards or CapEx reduction.
